title: Rust tests fail with 'Filename too long' and '$GIT_DIR too big' when the test temp root is deep (Windows path limits); about 166 tests on master c083c33
outcome: Rust tests fail with 'Filename too long' and '$GIT_DIR too big' when the test temp root is deep (Windows path limits); about 166 tests on master c083c33
acceptance: C1: Rust test fixture roots are named <prefix>-<16 lowercase hex> instead of a 36-char UUID. Each root is created exclusively, so a collision fails loudly. The owner marker and cleanup are unchanged. Path: src/test_temp_root.rs.

C2: on Windows, TestTempRoot::create refuses a root it would place in the default test_temp_dir() when that directory exceeds budget B, before it creates the root. The check is computed once per process, so every refused create fails with one identical message naming the directory, its length, B, and the remedy: set TERMAL_TEST_USER_TEMP shorter. Explicit TestTempRootDirectoryScope::within() directories and bare test_temp_dir() callers stay unchecked, which keeps the nested-temp contract tests intact. Non-Windows is unchanged. B = 67, from the recorded measurement: after C1 the deepest fixture GIT_DIR is 133 chars below the directory, with 20 chars of margin under GIT_DIR 220; the deepest file, at 156, stays under 260 with margin. The launcher default (46, or 57 with run-XXXXXX) fits. Paths: src/test_temp_paths.rs, src/test_temp_root.rs.

C2': on Windows, the same check and message, with the remedy 'use a shallower checkout', runs in TestTempRootDirectoryScope::repository_local() for the repository-local root (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/.tmp). Path: src/test_temp_root.rs.

C3: deterministic tests in src/tests/test_temp_paths.rs: (a) the budget check accepts a directory of exactly B and refuses one of B+1 with C2's message, for both entry points' remedies; (b) a Windows fixture at the C1 name under a directory padded to B runs git init, add and commit at the measured deepest depth; (c) on Windows, a child process whose default directory is over B has every TestTempRoot::create fail with the one identical message, and no root is created. No source scans, no timing.

C4: runtime RED of (b) and (c) on the master-root twin; GREEN on the candidate, on Windows. Plus one docs/test.md sentence near TERMAL_TEST_USER_TEMP stating the budget. No new gate stage and no launcher change.
The usual review pair (/review-changes) has no outstanding in-scope finding of Medium or higher, and the full gate is green on the exact landed input.

completion.summary:
Windows Rust test fixtures no longer fail with "Filename too long" or "$GIT_DIR too big" on a deep temp root.
- Fixture roots are named <prefix>-<16 hex> instead of a full UUID, which saves 20 chars, and are created exclusively.
- On Windows, a fixture root in the default test directory, or in the checkout's .tmp/, is refused with one clear message when that directory is longer than 67 bytes in canonical spelling. The budget was measured from a Git setup trace of the whole bin: the deepest fixture GIT_DIR is 133 below the directory, under Git's 220 limit with a 20-char margin.
- Tests (a), (b) and (c) cover the boundary, the deepest Git shape at the budget, and the single refusal. The docs give the effective TERMAL_TEST_USER_TEMP limits.

Evidence:
- Three review rounds, clean at round 3.
- RED R2, GREEN G4 and S4.
- The FULL on DL560 C6 (test-cfd64498) and the Windows whole bin (test-85638321).
- Pre-landing and post-landing evaluations both passed.

Landed as c4a26109 on master. The install was a no-op, with the binary identical, because the changes are test-only.
